ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-01.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-01.body:
Take side length 1. The hexagon is made of 6 equilateral triangles of side 1, each of area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}$, so its area is $\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}$. In triangle $CDF$, $CD=1$ and $DF=\sqrt3$ (a short diagonal), and $\angle CDF=90^\circ$ (since $\angle CDE=120^\circ$ and $\angle FDE=30^\circ$). So its area is $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$, and the ratio is $\frac{\sqrt3/2}{3\sqrt3/2}=\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-02.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-02.body:
Let the square have side $s$.

(a) The circle has radius $\frac s2$ so area $\frac{\pi s^2}{4}$. The ratio to $s^2$ is $\pi:4$, so $x=4$.

(b) The circle through the vertices has radius half the diagonal, $\frac{s\sqrt2}{2}$, so its area is $\frac{\pi s^2}{2}$ and the ratio is $\pi:2$, so $y=2$.

**Answer: (a) 4, (b) 2**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-03.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-03.body:
Write the grid as $\begin{array}{cc}a&b\\c&d\end{array}$. Then $\overline{ab}$, $\overline{cd}$, $\overline{ac}$, $\overline{bd}$ must all be two-digit squares with no zero digit: from $16,25,36,49,64,81$.

The first digit of each pair must start a square and the second digit end one. Trying the possibilities: $a=8$: $81$ across and $81$ down gives $b=1,c=1$, then $\overline{cd}=16$ and $\overline{bd}=16$ so $d=6$: digits $8,1,1,6$, sum 16. Other grids are $1,6,6,4$ (sum 17), $3,6,6,4$ (sum 19; $36,64,36,64$) and $6,4,4,9$ (sum 23; $64,49,64,49$). So the smallest sum is $16$ and the largest $23$.

**Answer: (a) 16, (b) 23**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-04.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-04.body:
The chambers form a grid of 4 rows and 3 columns. To get from the top left to the bottom right the mole must go down 3 times and across 2 times, which is 5 tunnels, so every route must have no backtracking. A route is an arrangement of 3 D's and 2 R's: $\binom52=10$.

**Answer: 10**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-05.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-05.body:
The 12 numbers total $1+2+3+5+6+\cdots+12+14=88$ and there are 4 rows, so every row and column sums to $22$. Name the unshaded cells row by row: $(1,p,x)$, $(q,r,s)$, $(2,t,u)$, $(v,w,3)$ (the shaded cells are on the diagonal). Rows 1, 3, 4 and columns 1, 2, 3 give $p+x=21$, $t+u=20$, $v+w=19$, $q+v=20$, $t+w=21$, $p+r=19$. Hence $x=r+2$, $w=u+1$, $q=w+1=u+2$ and $v=18-u$. From the available numbers $5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,14$: $u=8$ gives $w=9$, $q=10$, $v=10$ (repeat); $u=9$ gives $v=9$ (repeat); $u=11,12,14$ give a number above 14; so $u=6$, $w=7$, $q=8$, $v=12$, $t=14$. The remaining numbers $5,9,10,11$ go to $p,x,r,s$ with $x=r+2$, $p=19-r$: $r=9$, $x=11$, $p=10$, $s=5$. Check column 4: $11+5+6=22$.

**Answer: 11**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-06.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-06.body:
If $2n$ is not divisible by a square then $n$ is odd (else $4\mid 2n$ when $n$ even) and $n$ is square-free. So we need odd, square-free, composite $n$ between 2 and 50. Odd composites below 50: $9,15,21,25,27,33,35,39,45,49$. Remove those divisible by 9 or 25 or 49: $9,27,45,25,49$ go. Left: $15,21,33,35,39$, i.e. 5 numbers.

**Answer: 5**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-07.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-07.body:
Let the distance be $d$ miles. Cycling speed $=d/(16/60)=3.75d$ mph; walking speed $=d/(48/60)=1.25d$ mph. The difference is $2.5d=5$, so $d=2$.

**Answer: 2 miles**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-08.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-08.body:
A two-digit palindrome is $11a$, and $11a\times99=1089a$. The multiples are $1089, 2178, 3267, 4356, 5445, 6534, 7623, 8712, 9801$. Only $4356$ has tens digit 5.

**Answer: 4356**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-09.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-09.body:
(a) Let there be $b$ boys and $g$ girls. A son has $b-1$ brothers and $g$ sisters, so $b-1=g$. A daughter has $b$ brothers and $g-1$ sisters, so $b=2(g-1)$. Then $g+1=2g-2$, so $g=3$, $b=4$: 7 children.

(b) Let Hannah be $h$: $4h+20=2(h+20)$, so $2h=20$, $h=10$.

**Answer: (a) 7, (b) 10**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-10.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-group-10.body:
All five the same: HHHHH or TTTTT: 2 ways. Exactly four the same and one different: choose which child is different (5 ways) and which face it shows (2 ways): 10 ways. Total $2+10=12$.

**Answer: 12**
